# Good Plot vs Bad Plot
# Many Penguins!!!


```{r}
#| echo: TRUE

library(tidytuesdayR)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(ggfx)

```


## Load Data
```{r}

many_penguins <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-07-14/many_penguins.csv')

glimpse(many_penguins)
```
## Clean Data
```{r}

many_clean<-many_penguins|>
  filter(sex=="F", na.rm=TRUE)|>
  drop_na()

glimpse(many_clean)
```

## Good Plot
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| fig-cap: Correlation Between Wing and Tail Length in Female Penguins

Aptenodytes<- plot_ly( #plotly creates an interactive plot
  data = many_clean |> #requires very different code than ggplot
    filter(genus == "Aptenodytes"),
  x = ~tail.length,
  y = ~wing.length,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  name = "Aptenodytes",
  showlegend = TRUE, #run these on each graph so theres a complete legend when combined
  marker = list(size = 8, color="red"))|>
  layout(title = "Aptenodytes",
         xaxis = list(title = ""),
         yaxis = list(title = "Wing Length (mm)"))|>
  add_lines(showlegend=FALSE) #otherwise, will be a legend for each genus line?

Eudyptes<-plot_ly(
  data = many_clean |>
    filter(genus == "Eudyptes"),
  x = ~tail.length,
  y = ~wing.length,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  name = "Eudyptes",
  showlegend = TRUE,
  marker = list(size = 8, color="purple"))|>
  layout(title = "Eudyptes", #"layout" instead of "labs"
         xaxis = list(title = "Tail Length (mm)"),
         yaxis = list(title = ""))|>
  add_lines(showlegend=FALSE)

Pygoscelis<-plot_ly(
  data = many_clean |>
    filter(genus == "Pygoscelis"),
  x = ~tail.length,
  y = ~wing.length,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  name = "Pygoscelis",
  showlegend = TRUE,
  marker = list(size = 8, color="blue"))|>
  layout(title = "Pygoscelis",
         xaxis = list(title = ""),
         yaxis = list(title = ""))|>
  add_lines(y=~wing.length, showlegend=FALSE)

subplot(
  Aptenodytes, #adding the three plots together with ","
  Eudyptes,
  Pygoscelis,
  titleX = TRUE, #makes sure that axis titles are present
  titleY = TRUE
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "Female Penguins<br><sup>Tail Length vs Wing Length<sup>" 
    ),
      showlegend = TRUE,
    legend = list(
      title = list(text = "Genus")
    )
  )
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-penguins-pretty
#| fig-cap: Penguin Wing Length among Genus

good<- ggplot(data=many_penguins,
       mapping=aes(x=genus,y=wing.length, color=genus))+
  labs(title="Penguin Wing Length among Genus", x="Genus",y="Wing Length (mm)")+
  geom_boxplot()+
  guides(color="none")+
  theme_bw()


ggplotly(good) #converts ggplot to plotly


# couldn't figure out how to make a linear line like geom_smooth
```
The wing length among various penguin species within the six genus (Aptenodytes, Eudyptes, Eudyptula, Megadyptes, Pygoscelis, and Sphenicus) are represented in @fig-penguins-pretty. 

### What's good about this plot?

#### Clarity

* Presents raw data
* Not too many points, variables, or series
* No legend
* Simple and organized
  * Emphasis put on the six genus, instead of each species
* No special symbols or lines
  
#### Aesthetics

* Not cluttered
  * No unnecessary elements 
* Thoughtful color schemes
* Simple and legible fonts

## Bad Plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-penguins_ugly
#| fig-cap: No Idea What's Going on Here

bad_plot<- ggplot(data=many_penguins,
                     aes(x=tail.length,y=wing.length,
                     color=species))+ # species instead of genus makes it much more confusing
   labs(title="Penguins",x="Tail Length (in)",
       y="Wing Length (in)")+
         geom_boxplot(size=5)+ #make large un readable
  geom_smooth(method="lm", color="blue")+ #add line for fun, it tells us nothing
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "purple"), #ugly backdrop
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "pink"), #more ugly color
    element_text(family = "Apple Chancery"), #fabulous font everywhere
    plot.title = element_text(
      family = "Apple Chancery", #had to type this out for each axis, is there an easier way?
      size = 30,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(
      family = "Apple Chancery",
      size = 20 #unnecessarily big
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      family = "Apple Chancery",
      size = 20
    )
  )

bad_plot
ggsave(here("Week_8","outputs","bad_plot.png"))
```

In @fig-penguins_ugly, we can have a very hard time interpreting what is going on for a number of reasons... This plot seems to compare wing and tail across a number of penguin species. 

### What's bad about this plot?

#### Clarity

* There are too many data points
* The legend is overwhelming
* Nothing is put into context
* The title is vague and unclear
* There is an unnecessary trend line

#### Aesthetics

* Very cluttered
  * Boxes are too large and close together
* The coloring is distracting and confusing
  * Grid color and species colors
* Distracting and large font
  * Title font and legend font don't match
